prompt:
Choreographer Katherine Dunham studied anthropology as well as dance. She used field research in the Caribbean to inform performances that combined movement, music, and cultural history. Because her work joined artistic practice with academic study, Dunham’s career is often described as ______.
Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word?
explanation: Dunham’s work combined dance with anthropology and cultural research, so “interdisciplinary” is the most precise choice.

prompt:
Some farmers plant cover crops after the main harvest. Cover crops such as clover or rye can protect bare soil from erosion, add organic matter, and reduce weed growth before the next planting season. Although these crops may not be sold, they can still improve the health of a field.
Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Cover crops can improve soil conditions even when they are not grown for sale.
choices.B: Cover crops are planted only because they produce the most valuable harvests.
choices.C: Bare soil is always healthier than soil covered by plants.
choices.D: Clover and rye prevent farmers from planting other crops later.

explanation: The passage explains that cover crops protect soil, add organic matter, and reduce weeds even though they may not be sold.

prompt:

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The singular subject “group” requires the singular verb “is.”

prompt:
A student recorded the number of visitors to four displays at a history night event.
Display | Visitors
Railroad maps | 44
Military letters | 38
School photographs | 52
Farm tools | 47
Which choice is supported by the data in the table?

choices.A: The School photographs display had the greatest number of visitors.
choices.B: The Military letters display had more visitors than the Farm tools display.
choices.C: The Railroad maps and School photographs displays had the same number of visitors.
choices.D: No display had more than 47 visitors.

explanation: The School photographs display had 52 visitors, more than the other displays.

prompt:
Evan wanted to solve the puzzle as quickly as possible, so he guessed at each answer without reading the clues carefully. After several wrong attempts, he slowed down and began underlining important words. The next solution took longer, but it was correct.

choices.A: Evan becomes more successful when he pays closer attention.
choices.B: Evan stops working on the puzzle because he dislikes clues.
choices.C: Evan proves that guessing is always better than reading carefully.
choices.D: Evan creates a new puzzle for other students to solve.

prompt:
In a passage about ancient Roman roads, a historian explains that stone markers were placed at intervals along important routes. The historian adds, “These markers could show distances to nearby towns, helping travelers estimate how far they still needed to go.”

choices.A: It explains a practical use of stone markers along Roman roads.
choices.B: It argues that Roman travelers never visited nearby towns.
choices.C: It describes how stones were cut from quarries.
choices.D: It shows that ancient roads were built without planning.

explanation: The quoted sentence explains that markers helped travelers estimate distances.

prompt:

explanation: The second sentence adds another use of the school greenhouse.

prompt:

choices.B: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1983.
choices.C: Stars can be studied by scientists using many different methods.
choices.D: A white dwarf is one type of object found in space.

prompt:

explanation: The sentence contrasts the usefulness of quick score access with students’ preference for explanatory written comments.

explanation: Sentence 2 logically explains what participants bring before the paragraph describes benefits of the exchange.

prompt:

prompt:
Some schools run uniform closets, where families can donate clean shirts, jackets, or pants that no longer fit. Other students can then take needed items at no cost. These closets can reduce waste while helping families meet school clothing requirements.

choices.B: Uniform closets require families to buy new clothing before donating anything.
choices.C: Donated clothing can never be used by other students.
choices.D: School clothing requirements are always easier to meet without donated items.

explanation: The passage explains that uniform closets provide no-cost clothing and reduce waste.

prompt:
Scientists studying desert tortoises note that the animals spend much of the hottest part of the day in burrows. These underground spaces are cooler than the surface and help the tortoises avoid overheating.
According to the text, why do desert tortoises use burrows during the hottest part of the day?

choices.A: To stay cooler and avoid overheating
choices.B: To collect food from tree branches
choices.C: To make the desert surface hotter
choices.D: To build nests above the ground

explanation: The text states that burrows are cooler than the surface and help tortoises avoid overheating.
